Overview

Tbilisi as a Business Centre

Tbilisi is Georgia's capital and the country's dominant business centre. According to Geostat, about 1.3 million people, roughly 35 percent of the national population, lived in the city on 1 January 2025, and Tbilisi generated 53.1 percent of Georgia's GDP in 2024. Wholesale and retail trade, real estate activities and construction are the largest contributors to the city's value added. Tbilisi hosts the national government, the main commercial banks, the Georgian Stock Exchange, the Georgian International Arbitration Centre and the Tbilisi Free Industrial Zone. Its location makes it a base for companies trading between Europe, Turkey, the South Caucasus, Central Asia and Russia.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Tbilisi for reasons tied to that position. Inflows of foreign residents and businesses since 2022 have brought many newly formed companies with foreign shareholders, making it important to establish who stands behind a counterparty. Construction and real estate dominate local investment, and buyers and lenders need to understand developers, land titles and related parties. Traders and logistics firms routing goods through Georgia face scrutiny over export controls and sanctions diversion, so their partners need careful screening. Investors in Georgian groups, and parties in disputes before Tbilisi courts or in arbitration, need well-documented facts about ownership, assets and conduct.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Tbilisi

01

Foreign-owned company backgrounds

Researching recently formed Tbilisi companies with foreign founders, including shareholders and directors of record, prior businesses abroad, adverse media and litigation, so that banks, partners and investors can establish who actually controls a counterparty before onboarding or contracting.

02

Real estate and developer diligence

Background research on Tbilisi developers, contractors and investors, covering ownership, related companies, registered property rights and mortgages, litigation and project history, to help buyers, lenders and joint venture partners assess delivery risk, encumbrances and conflicts of interest.

03

Transit trade counterparty screening

Screening logistics firms, re-exporters and trading houses based in Tbilisi for ownership links, trade patterns and adverse media that may indicate sanctions or export-control diversion, supporting compliance teams that must justify continued business with Caucasus intermediaries over time.

04

Acquisition and investor diligence

Ownership, management and reputational research on Georgian groups before acquisitions, minority investments or financing, including political exposure of shareholders, related-party transactions and regulatory history, presented in clear English with clear source references for investment committees.

05

Asset research for disputes

Locating lawfully documented property, company interests and pledges of Georgian counterparties for creditors and counsel pursuing claims in Tbilisi courts or GIAC arbitration, and identifying transfers of assets to related parties before or during proceedings.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Tbilisi

Courts sitting in Tbilisi

Commercial disputes involving Tbilisi companies are commonly heard at first instance by the Tbilisi City Court, with appeals to the Tbilisi Court of Appeals, and the Supreme Court of Georgia also sits in the capital. Litigation history before these courts is a key indicator of a counterparty's disputes and creditor pressure, and counsel can advise on access to case information and filings.

Georgian International Arbitration Centre

GIAC was founded in December 2013 on the initiative of the Georgian Chamber of Commerce and Industry and operates as an independent non-profit institution at 29 Shataidze Street, Tbilisi. It replaced the chamber's former arbitration court, suspended in 2012, and describes itself as the first international arbitration institution in the region. It hosts the annual Tbilisi Arbitration Days and offers both its own rules and UNCITRAL Rules administration.

Tbilisi Free Industrial Zone

The Tbilisi Free Industrial Zone, also known as the Tbilisi Technology Park, lies near the city centre and the international airport. Companies licensed in it can obtain tax advantages under Georgia's free zone rules, which have attracted trading and service companies with limited physical presence. Diligence on such entities confirms their licence, actual activity and owners rather than relying on a free zone address.

Financial and capital markets institutions

The Georgian Stock Exchange, founded in 1999, is the country's principal exchange and is based in Tbilisi, as are the major commercial banks and the Georgian Chamber of Commerce and Industry. Listed issuers and banks publish disclosures that help verify ownership and financial standing, though the local listed market is small and most companies are privately held. Bank and issuer disclosures are therefore read alongside registry data.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Tbilisi

For matters touching Tbilisi, TDSC first defines the question, whether that is the real owner of a new company, the reliability of a developer, a transit trader's links or a debtor's assets, and then identifies the relevant records, including registry and property data, court decisions and Georgian and Russian-language press. Research is conducted from Nashville, with Turkish, Russian and Central Asian sources where a counterparty's history lies abroad. Every matter is screened for US and other applicable sanctions before work begins. Where site visits, interviews or certified records are needed, TDSC coordinates with appropriately qualified local professionals and the client's Georgian counsel, and personal data is handled under Georgia's data protection law.

TDSC has no office in Tbilisi. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Tbilisi: Frequently Asked Questions

How do we identify who really owns a recently formed Tbilisi company?

We start with the registry record of founders, partners and directors, then trace those individuals and entities through foreign registries, prior companies, litigation and media. Where a nominee or foreign holding company appears, we report how far ownership can be traced from lawful sources and recommend contractual disclosures or further steps through counsel.

Can you check a Tbilisi developer before we buy or lend?

Yes. We review the developer's ownership, related companies, completed and stalled projects, registered rights and mortgages over relevant plots, litigation and adverse media. Title opinions and formal property searches remain matters for Georgian counsel and notaries; our work identifies risks they should examine. We also note any disputes with buyers or contractors.

Do you screen Georgian trading partners for sanctions diversion risk?

We research ownership, management links, trade activity and adverse media for Tbilisi-based logistics and trading companies, and look for connections to sanctioned persons or patterns consistent with diversion. Our findings support, but do not replace, the client's sanctions and export-control compliance decisions and legal advice.

Can TDSC support a GIAC arbitration or Tbilisi court case?

We can assemble documented facts about the opposing party, its owners, assets and history of disputes, and help counsel trace transfers to related parties. We do not act as counsel or give legal advice, and any evidence intended for proceedings is gathered with counsel's direction so that it can be used properly.

Does TDSC have an office in Tbilisi?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Georgia. Most of our work is desk-based research from public and commercial sources. Where local steps are justified, we coordinate with appropriately qualified local professionals and the client's Georgian counsel, and we do not use covert or deceptive methods.
